nodes.name: Cyclic weighted polymorphism is necessary for tractability
nodes.statement: In recent work on the tractability of valued constraint languages, it has been shown that a necessary condition for tractability is the existence of a \emph{cyclic} weighted polymorphism~\cite{Kozik15:icalp}.\footnote{A $k$-ary operation if \emph{cyclic} if $f(x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_k)=f(x_2,\ldots,x_k,x_1)$ for every $x_1,\ldots,x_k$. A weighting $\omega$ is cyclic if every operation $f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)$ is cyclic.}
conclusions:
a necessary condition for tractability is the existence of a
\emph{cyclic} weighted polymorphism

nodes.name: Cyclic weighted polymorphism is sufficient under Feder-Vardi
nodes.statement: Moreover, it has been also shown that, under the assumption of the dichotomy conjecture of Feder and Vardi for the decision problem, this condition is also sufficient~\cite{Kolmogorov15:general-valued}.
assumptions:
under the
assumption of the dichotomy conjecture of Feder and Vardi for the decision
problem

nodes.name: Define cyclic sum $\omega'$
nodes.statement: Let \begin{equation} \omega'\ =\ \sum_{\pi\in\mathrm{Cycl}_k}\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(k)}_{\pi(1)},\ldots,\ensuremath{e}^{(k)}_{\pi(k)}]\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Define $\omega'$ as the sum of superpositions with cyclic permutations of projections.

nodes.name: Cyclic invariance of $\omega'$
nodes.statement: Let $f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)$ and $\pi\in\mathrm{Cycl}_k$. We have \begin{multline} \omega'(f)\ =\ \sum_{g\in{\rm supp}(\omega)}\ \sum_{\substack{\text{$\sigma\in\mathrm{Cycl}_k$}\\\text{$g^{\sigma}=f$}}}\omega(g) \ =\ \sum_{g\in{\rm supp}(\omega)}\ \sum_{\substack{\text{$\sigma\circ\pi\in\mathrm{Cycl}_k$}\\\text{$g^{\sigma\circ\pi}=f^\pi$}}}\omega(g) \ =\ \\ \ =\ \sum_{g\in{\rm supp}(\omega)}\ \sum_{\substack{\text{$\sigma'\in\mathrm{Cycl}_k$}\\\text{$g^{\sigma'}=f^\pi$}}}\omega(g) \ = \ \omega'(f^\pi)\,. \end{multline} Thus $\omega'$ satisfies the first and the third property of the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Reindex the sum to show $\omega'(f)=\omega'(f^\pi)$.

nodes.name: Negative projection weights
nodes.statement: Since $\omega$ is positive we have that $\sum_{i=1}^k\omega(\ensuremath{e}^{(k)}_i)<0$ and thus, by~\eqref{eq:long}, we have $\omega'(\ensuremath{e}^{(k)}_i)<0$ for every $1\leq i\leq k$.
nodes.statement_short: Positivity forces every projection to get negative weight under $\omega'$.

nodes.name: Normalise
nodes.statement: Let $\omega'(\ensuremath{e}^{(k)}_1)=w$. By~\eqref{eq:long} again, $\omega'(\ensuremath{e}^{(k)}_i)=w$ for every $1\leq i\leq k$. Thus $\mu=\frac{1}{w}\omega'$ satisfies all three properties of the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: All projections share weight $w$; rescale by $1/w$.

nodes.name: Normalised unary weighting
nodes.statement: Let $\omega\in\mathrm{wPol}(\Gamma)$ be a positive unary weighting. By scaling by $1/|\omega(\ensuremath{e}^{(1)}_1)|$, we have $\omega(\ensuremath{e}^{(1)}_1)=-1$ and thus $\sum_{f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)}\omega(f)=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Take a positive unary weighted polymorphism, scaled so the projection has weight $-1$.

nodes.name: Weighted polymorphism inequality $(\ast)$
nodes.statement: For any weighted relation $\phi\in\Gamma$ of arity $m$ and any $m$-tuple $\tup{x}\in D^m$, we have $(\ast)$ $\phi(\tup{x})\geq\sum_{f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)}\omega(f)\phi(f(\tup{x}))$.
nodes.statement_short: Derive $(\ast)$: $\phi(x)$ dominates the $\omega$-average over images.

nodes.name: Images of optimal assignments are optimal
nodes.statement: Suppose that $\tup{y}$ is a minimal-cost assignment for $\phi$; that is, $\phi(\tup{y})\leq\phi(\tup{x})$ for all $\tup{x}\in D^m$. Then for every $f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)$, we have $f(\tup{y})$ is also a minimal-cost assignment.
nodes.statement_short: State that every $f$ in the support maps an optimal assignment to an optimal one.

nodes.name: Assume a worse image
nodes.statement: Assume for contrary that for some $f'\in{\rm supp}(\omega)$, we have $\phi(f'(\tup{y}))>\phi(\tup{y})$; write $\phi(f'(\tup{y}))=\phi(\tup{y})+\epsilon$, where $\epsilon>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Suppose some $f'$ strictly increases the cost by $\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Claim: some image is strictly better
nodes.statement: Then we claim that there is an $f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)$ such that $\phi(f(\tup{y}))<\phi(\tup{y})$, which contradicts the choice of $\tup{y}$. To prove the claim assume that $\phi(f(\tup{y}))\geq\phi(\tup{y})$ for every $f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)\setminus\{f'\}$. Hence we get $\sum_{f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)}\omega(f)\phi(f(\tup{y})) = \sum_{f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)\setminus\{f'\}}\omega(f)\phi(f(\tup{y}))+\omega(f')\phi(f'(\tup{y})) \geq (1-\omega(f')\phi(\tup{y})+\omega(f')(\phi(\tup{y})+\epsilon) = \phi(\tup{y})+\omega(f')\epsilon>\phi(\tup{y})$, which contradicts $(\ast)$.
nodes.statement_short: Show some other $f$ would give a strictly better assignment, a contradiction.

nodes.name: Assume no better image
nodes.statement: To prove the claim assume that $\phi(f(\tup{y}))\geq\phi(\tup{y})$ for every $f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)\setminus\{f'\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume all other images are at least as costly.

nodes.name: Weighted average exceeds $\phi(y)$
nodes.statement: Hence we get $\sum_{f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)}\omega(f)\phi(f(\tup{y})) = \sum_{f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)\setminus\{f'\}}\omega(f)\phi(f(\tup{y}))+\omega(f')\phi(f'(\tup{y})) \geq (1-\omega(f')\phi(\tup{y})+\omega(f')(\phi(\tup{y})+\epsilon) = \phi(\tup{y})+\omega(f')\epsilon>\phi(\tup{y})$, which contradicts $(\ast)$.
nodes.statement_short: The weighted average then exceeds $\phi(y)$, contradicting $(\ast)$.

nodes.name: Solutions map to solutions
nodes.statement: Consequently, given an instance $I\in\mathrm{VCSP}(\Gamma)$ and a solution $s$ to $I$, we can take any unary weighting $\omega\in\mathrm{wPol}(\Gamma)$ and any unary operation $f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)$ and get another solution $f(s)$ to $I$; the solution $f(s)$ uses only labels from $f(D)$.
nodes.statement_short: Applying a support operation to a solution gives a solution using labels from $f(D)$.

nodes.name: Restricted language $\Gamma'$
nodes.statement: Consider a unary non-bijective operation $f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)$ with the minimum $|f(D)|$ over all unary weightings $\omega\in\mathrm{wPol}(\Gamma)$. We denote by $D'=f(D)$ the range of $f$. We denote by $\Gamma'$ language containing the restriction of every $\phi\in\Gamma$ to $D'$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose a non-bijective unary $f$ with smallest image $D'$ and restrict $\Gamma$ to $D'$.

nodes.name: Polynomial reduction and iteration
nodes.statement: Given any instance $I\in\mathrm{VCSP}(\Gamma)$ we can create, by replacing each weighted relation $\phi$ in $I$ by $\phi'$, in polynomial time an instance $I'\in\mathrm{VCSP}(\Gamma')$ with the following properties: any solution to $I'$ is also a solution to $I$, and for any solution $s$ to $I$ we have that $f(s)$ is a solution to $I'$. If $\Gamma'$ is not a core we can repeat the same construction with $\Gamma'$.
nodes.statement_short: Instances of $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma'$ reduce to each other; iterate until a core.

nodes.name: Symmetrise via Lemma 2
nodes.statement: Let $\omega$ be $k$-ary. Note that if $f$ is a $k$-ary near-unanimity operation then so is $g(x_1,\ldots,x_k)=f(x_{\pi(1)},\ldots,x_{\pi(k)})$ for any permutation $\pi$ on $\{1,\ldots,k\}$. Thus, by Lemma~\ref{lem:perm}, we can assume $\omega$ assigns weight $-1$ to each of the $k$ projections (and still every $f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)$ is a near-unanimity operation).
nodes.statement_short: Use permutation-closure of near-unanimity and Lemma 2 to assume weight $-1$ on each projection.

nodes.name: First inequality
nodes.statement: Let $\phi\in\mathrm{Imp}(W)$ be an $m$-ary weighted relation and let $\tup{x},\tup{y}\in D^m$ be such that $\tup{x},\tup{y}\in{Feas}(\phi)$. Since $\omega\in\mathrm{wPol}(\phi)$, we have, by~\eqref{eq:WPOL} with $\tup{x}_1=\tup{y}$ and $\tup{x}_i=\tup{x}$ for all $2\leq i\leq k$, and by~\eqref{eq:defNU}, $-\phi(\tup{y})-(k-1)\phi(\tup{x})+k\phi(\tup{x})\leq 0$, which gives $\phi(\tup{x})\leq\phi(\tup{y})$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the weighted polymorphism inequality with one $y$ and $k-1$ copies of $x$.

nodes.name: Second inequality
nodes.statement: By swapping $\tup{x}$ and $\tup{y}$ in~\eqref{eq:WPOL}, we get $-\phi(\tup{x})-(k-1)\phi(\tup{y})+k\phi(\tup{y})\leq 0$, which gives $\phi(\tup{y})\leq\phi(\tup{x})$.
nodes.statement_short: Swap roles to get the reverse inequality.

nodes.name: Constant on feasible set
nodes.statement: Together, $\phi(\tup{x})=\phi(\tup{y})$ for all $\tup{x},\tup{y}\in{Feas}(\phi)$.
nodes.statement_short: $\phi$ is constant on its feasible tuples, so $W$ is crisp.

nodes.name: Symmetrise via Lemma 2
nodes.statement: Note that if $f$ is a minority operation then so is $g(x_1,x_2,x_3)=f(x_{\pi(1)},x_{\pi(2)},x_{\pi(3)})$ for any permutation $\pi$ on $\{1,2,3\}$. Thus, by Lemma~\ref{lem:perm}, we can assume $\omega$ assigns weight $-1$ to each of the three projections (and still every $f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)$ is a minority operation).
nodes.statement_short: Minority is closed under permutations, so by Lemma 2 assume weight $-1$ on each projection.

nodes.name: First inequality
nodes.statement: Let $\phi\in\mathrm{Imp}(W)$ be an $m$-ary weighted relation and let $\tup{x},\tup{y}\in D^m$ be such that $\tup{x},\tup{y}\in{Feas}(\phi)$. Since $\omega\in\mathrm{wPol}(\phi)$, we have, by~\eqref{eq:WPOL} with $\tup{x}_1=\tup{x}$ and $\tup{x}_2=\tup{x}_3=\tup{y}$, $-\phi(\tup{x})-2\phi(\tup{y})+3\phi(\tup{x})\leq 0$, which gives $\phi(\tup{x})\leq\phi(\tup{y})$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the weighted polymorphism inequality to $(x,y,y)$.

nodes.name: Second inequality
nodes.statement: By swapping $\tup{x}$ and $\tup{y}$ in~\eqref{eq:WPOL}, we get $-\phi(\tup{y})-2\phi(\tup{x})+3\phi(\tup{y})\leq 0$, which gives $\phi(\tup{y})\leq\phi(\tup{x})$.
nodes.statement_short: Swap roles to get the reverse inequality.

nodes.name: Constant on feasible set
nodes.statement: Together, $\phi(\tup{x})=\phi(\tup{y})$ for all $\tup{x},\tup{y}\in{Feas}(\phi)$.
nodes.statement_short: $\phi$ is constant on feasible tuples, so $W$ is crisp.

nodes.name: Symmetrise via Lemma 2
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:perm}, we can assume the weighting assigns weight $-1$ to each of the three projections and still is as described in Theorem~\ref{thm:class2}\,(2c). An $m$-ary relation $R$ on $D$ is called trivial if $R=D^m$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume the (2c) weighting has weight $-1$ on each projection; call $D^m$ trivial.

nodes.name: Claim: relations in $\mathcal{R}$ decompose
nodes.statement: First we show than any relation $R\in\mathcal{R}$ can be expressed as a sum of unary relations, trivial relations, and $\phi_=$. The claim holds true for the generators of $\mathcal{R}$, that is, for $\phi_=$ and $\phi_d$ for all $d\in D$. Next, if $R=R_1\wedge R_2$ and the claim holds true for both $R_1$ and $R_2$ the it also holds true for $R$. Finally, let $R=\exists x R'$ and assume that $R'$ satisfies the claim. If $x$ appears in some $\phi_=$ in $R'$, say $\phi_=(x,x')$, then we can replace all occurrences of $x$ by $x'$. Otherwise, $x$ appears only in constant and trivial relations in $R'$. If the conjunction of the unary relations that $x$ appears in is empty then the claim holds trivially. Otherwise, we can replace $x$ by any other variable.
nodes.statement_short: Structural induction over generators, conjunction and projection of $\mathcal{R}$.

nodes.name: Generators
nodes.statement: The claim holds true for the generators of $\mathcal{R}$, that is, for $\phi_=$ and $\phi_d$ for all $d\in D$.
nodes.statement_short: Base case: generators $\phi_=$ and $\phi_d$.

nodes.name: Conjunction
nodes.statement: Next, if $R=R_1\wedge R_2$ and the claim holds true for both $R_1$ and $R_2$ the it also holds true for $R$.
nodes.statement_short: Conjunction preserves the decomposition.

nodes.name: Existential quantification
nodes.statement: Finally, let $R=\exists x R'$ and assume that $R'$ satisfies the claim. If $x$ appears in some $\phi_=$ in $R'$, say $\phi_=(x,x')$, then we can replace all occurrences of $x$ by $x'$. Otherwise, $x$ appears only in constant and trivial relations in $R'$. If the conjunction of the unary relations that $x$ appears in is empty then the claim holds trivially. Otherwise, we can replace $x$ by any other variable.
nodes.statement_short: Eliminate the quantified variable via equality or unary constraints.

nodes.name: Reduce to trivial feasibility
nodes.statement: Consequently, for any $\phi\in\mathrm{Imp}(W)$, $\mathrm{Feas}(\phi)$ can be written as a sum of unary relations, trivial relations, and $\phi_=$. Observe that any $\phi$ with $\mathrm{Feas}(\phi)=\phi_=$ can be written as a sum of $\phi_=$ and the unary weighted relation $\phi'(x)=\phi(x,x)$. Thus, it remains to show that any $\phi\in\mathrm{Imp}(W)$ with $\mathrm{Feas}(\phi)$ being a trivial relation can be written as a sum of unary weighted relations.
nodes.statement_short: Handle equality-feasible relations; it remains to treat trivially feasible ones.

nodes.name: Substitution notation
nodes.statement: For any $m$-tuple $\tup{x}\in D^m$, we will write $\tup{x}[i\leftarrow d]$ to denote the tuple with $d\in D$ {substituted} at position $i$. In other words, $\tup{x}[i\leftarrow d]$ is the $m$-tuple identical to $\tup{x}$ except (possibly) at position $i$, where it is equal to $d$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $x[i\leftarrow d]$.

nodes.name: First exchange inequality
nodes.statement: Take any $\tup{x},\tup{y}\in D^m$ and $1\leq i\leq m$. Let $a=\tup{x}[i]$ and $b=\tup{y}[i]$. Now consider the tuples $\tup{x}$, $\tup{x}[i\leftarrow b]$, and $\tup{y}[i\leftarrow a]$. By applying the weighting from the statement of the proposition as in~\eqref{eq:WPOL}, we get $\phi(\tup{x})+\phi(\tup{x}[i\leftarrow b])+\phi(\tup{y}[i\leftarrow a]) \geq 2\phi(\tup{x})+\phi(\tup{y})$ and thus $\phi(\tup{x}[i\leftarrow b])+\phi(\tup{y}[i\leftarrow a]) \geq \phi(\tup{x})+\phi(\tup{y})$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the weighting to $x$, $x[i\leftarrow b]$, $y[i\leftarrow a]$ to get one inequality.

nodes.name: Second exchange inequality
nodes.statement: Now consider the tuples $\tup{x}$, $\tup{y}$, and $\tup{y}[i\leftarrow a]$. By applying the weighting from the statement of the proposition as in~\eqref{eq:WPOL}, we get $\phi(\tup{x})+\phi(\tup{y})+\phi(\tup{y}[i\leftarrow a]) \geq 2\phi(\tup{y}[i\leftarrow a]) + \phi(\tup{x}[i\leftarrow b])$ and thus $\phi(\tup{x})+\phi(\tup{y}) \geq \phi(\tup{y}[i\leftarrow a]) + \phi(\tup{x}[i\leftarrow b])$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply it to $x$, $y$, $y[i\leftarrow a]$ for the reverse inequality, giving the identity.

nodes.name: All finite-valued relations
nodes.statement: If $\Gamma$ contains all finite-valued weighted relations then it is intractable.
nodes.statement_short: If all finite-valued relations are in $\Gamma$, it is intractable.

nodes.name: Some finite-valued relation missing
nodes.statement: Otherwise, there is a finite-valued weighted relation $\phi\not\in\Gamma$. Since $\phi$ is finite-valued we have $\mathrm{Feas}(\Gamma)=\mathrm{Feas}(\mathrm{wRelClone}(\Gamma\cup\{\phi\}))$. But then either $\mathrm{Feas}(\Gamma)=\mathbf{R}_D$, in which case $\Gamma$ is intractable, or $\mathrm{Feas}(\Gamma)=\mathrm{Feas}(\mathrm{wRelClone}(\Gamma\cup\{\phi\}))\neq\mathbf{R}_D$, in which case $\Gamma$ is not maximal.
nodes.statement_short: Adding a missing finite-valued $\phi$ keeps the feasibility relations, so $\Gamma$ is intractable or not maximal.

nodes.name: Setup and notation
nodes.statement: It suffices to consider the ternary case as the rest of the theorem follows from (the proof of) Theorem~\ref{thm:class1} and the fact that $W$ is a rigid core, which eliminates the first case of Theorem~\ref{thm:class1}. Let $W$ be a weighted clone containing a ternary positive weighting $\omega$ such that every $f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)$ is sharp. (If some $f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)$ were not sharp then we could show, as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:class1}, that the case~(1) holds.) We denote by $C$ the support clone of $W$. We assume that none of the cases (2a), (2b), (2c), (3) (with $k=3$) of the theorem applies as we would be done in any of these cases. By Lemma~\ref{lem:perm}, we can assume that $\omega$ assigns weight $-1$ to each of the three ternary projections and thus \begin{equation} \sum_{f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)}\omega(f)\ =\ 3\,. \end{equation} Let $P_i\subseteq C$ be the Pixley operations of type $i\in\{1,2,3\}$ from $C$. Since $C$ is a clone we have \begin{equation} |P_1|\ =\ |P_2|\ =\ |P_3|\,. \end{equation} By Lemma~\ref{lem:perm}, we have for any three related Pixley operations $p_1\in P_1$, $p_2\in P_2$, and $p_3\in P_3$, \begin{equation} \omega(p_1)\ =\ \omega(p_2)\ =\ \omega(p_3)\,, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \sum_{p\in P_1} \omega(p)\ =\ \sum_{p\in P_2} \omega(p)\ =\ \sum_{p\in P_3} \omega(p)\,. \end{equation} We set $P=P_1\cup P_2\cup P_3$ to be the set of all Pixley operations from $C$ and $w(P)=\sum_{p\in P}\omega(p)$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:perm}, the same holds for the three types of ternary semiprojections. In particular, we denote by $S_i\subseteq C$ the operations from $C$ that are semiprojections of type $i\in\{1,2,3\}$. Since $C$ is a clone, we have \begin{equation} |S_1|\ =\ |S_2|\ =\ |S_3|\,. \end{equation} For any three related semiprojections $s_1\in S_1$, $s_2\in S_2$, and $s_3\in S_3$, \begin{equation} \omega(s_1)\ =\ \omega(s_2)\ =\ \omega(s_3)\,, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \sum_{s\in S_1} \omega(s)\ =\ \sum_{s\in S_2} \omega(s)\ =\ \sum_{s\in S_3} \omega(s)\,. \end{equation} We set $S=S_1\cup S_2\cup S_3$ to be the set of all semiprojections from $C$ and $w(S)=\sum_{s\in S}\omega(s)$. To simplify the presentation, we use the same notation for weightings, index sets, etc. in the following three steps since the steps are similar (but independent). Thus, for example, when one reads $J$ in Step II it refers to $J$ defined in Step II and not in Step I.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a symmetric ternary sharp weighting and introduce the Pixley and semiprojection classes.

nodes.name: Reduce to ternary case
nodes.statement: It suffices to consider the ternary case as the rest of the theorem follows from (the proof of) Theorem~\ref{thm:class1} and the fact that $W$ is a rigid core, which eliminates the first case of Theorem~\ref{thm:class1}.
nodes.statement_short: Other cases follow from Theorem 4 and rigidity.

nodes.name: Ternary sharp weighting
nodes.statement: Let $W$ be a weighted clone containing a ternary positive weighting $\omega$ such that every $f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)$ is sharp. (If some $f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)$ were not sharp then we could show, as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:class1}, that the case~(1) holds.) We denote by $C$ the support clone of $W$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix $W$, a ternary positive weighting with sharp support, and its support clone $C$.

nodes.name: Assume no target case holds
nodes.statement: We assume that none of the cases (2a), (2b), (2c), (3) (with $k=3$) of the theorem applies as we would be done in any of these cases.
nodes.statement_short: Assume none of (2a), (2b), (2c), (3) applies.

nodes.name: Normalise via Lemma 2
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:perm}, we can assume that $\omega$ assigns weight $-1$ to each of the three ternary projections and thus \begin{equation} \sum_{f\in{\rm supp}(\omega)}\omega(f)\ =\ 3\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Projections get weight $-1$, so total positive weight is 3.

nodes.name: Pixley classes
nodes.statement: Let $P_i\subseteq C$ be the Pixley operations of type $i\in\{1,2,3\}$ from $C$. Since $C$ is a clone we have \begin{equation} |P_1|\ =\ |P_2|\ =\ |P_3|\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Define $P_i$ and note they have equal sizes.

nodes.name: Related Pixley weights
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:perm}, we have for any three related Pixley operations $p_1\in P_1$, $p_2\in P_2$, and $p_3\in P_3$, \begin{equation} \omega(p_1)\ =\ \omega(p_2)\ =\ \omega(p_3)\,, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \sum_{p\in P_1} \omega(p)\ =\ \sum_{p\in P_2} \omega(p)\ =\ \sum_{p\in P_3} \omega(p)\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Related Pixley operations get equal weight and the type sums agree.

nodes.name: Total Pixley weight
nodes.statement: We set $P=P_1\cup P_2\cup P_3$ to be the set of all Pixley operations from $C$ and $w(P)=\sum_{p\in P}\omega(p)$.
nodes.statement_short: Define $P$ and $w(P)$.

nodes.name: Semiprojection classes
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:perm}, the same holds for the three types of ternary semiprojections. In particular, we denote by $S_i\subseteq C$ the operations from $C$ that are semiprojections of type $i\in\{1,2,3\}$. Since $C$ is a clone, we have \begin{equation} |S_1|\ =\ |S_2|\ =\ |S_3|\,. \end{equation} For any three related semiprojections $s_1\in S_1$, $s_2\in S_2$, and $s_3\in S_3$, \begin{equation} \omega(s_1)\ =\ \omega(s_2)\ =\ \omega(s_3)\,, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \sum_{s\in S_1} \omega(s)\ =\ \sum_{s\in S_2} \omega(s)\ =\ \sum_{s\in S_3} \omega(s)\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Define $S_i$ with the analogous size and weight equalities.

nodes.name: Total semiprojection weight
nodes.statement: We set $S=S_1\cup S_2\cup S_3$ to be the set of all semiprojections from $C$ and $w(S)=\sum_{s\in S}\omega(s)$.
nodes.statement_short: Define $S$ and $w(S)$.

nodes.name: Notation convention
nodes.statement: To simplify the presentation, we use the same notation for weightings, index sets, etc. in the following three steps since the steps are similar (but independent). Thus, for example, when one reads $J$ in Step II it refers to $J$ defined in Step II and not in Step I.
nodes.statement_short: Notation is reused independently across the three steps.

nodes.name: Step I: eliminating Pixley operations
nodes.statement: \textbf{Step I}: Eliminating Pixley operations. We now show how to eliminate Pixley operations if needed, that is, assume $w(P)>0$ and thus some operations from $P$ are assigned positive weight. First assume that $\omega$ assigns positive weight to only Pixley operations, that is, ${\rm supp}(\omega)\subseteq P$. Hence $w(P)=3$. Take arbitrary $p_1,p'_1\in P_1$, $p_2,p'_2\in P_2$, and $p_3,p'_3\in P_3$. The following claims can be verified from the definitions: $p_1[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,p'_1]$ is a majority operation, $p_2[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,p'_1]=\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1$, and $p_3[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,p'_1]=\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2$. Consequently, $\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,p'_1]$ assigns weight $-1$ to $p'_1$, $+1$ to majority operations, and $0$ otherwise. Similarly, $\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,p'_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3]$ assigns weight $-1$ to $p'_2$, $+1$ to majority operations, and $0$ otherwise. Finally, $\omega[p'_3,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3]$ assigns weight $-1$ to $p'_3$, $+1$ to majority operations, and $0$ otherwise. Overall, the weighting \begin{equation} \mu\ =\ \omega+\sum_{p\in P_1}\omega(p)\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,p] +\sum_{p\in P_2}\omega(p)\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,p,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3] +\sum_{p\in P_3}\omega(p)\omega[p,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3] \end{equation} assigns weight $-1$ to each of the three ternary projections and weight $3$ to majority operations. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:sumofsuperpos}, the intermediate superpositions in~\eqref{eq:pixleyonly} can be improper as long as the resulting weighting $\mu$ is indeed a weighting. Thus $\mu\in W$ and case~(2a) of the theorem holds. Let assume that ${\rm supp}(\omega)\not\subseteq P$, that is, $\omega$ assigns positive weight not only to Pixley operations. Let $J=\{(p_1,p_2,p_3)\in P_1\times P_2\times P_3\:|\:\mbox{$p_1, p_2, p_3$ are related}\}$ and $\bar{J}=\{(\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3)\}\cup J$. We consider the following linear system: for all Pixley operations $p\in P$, \begin{equation} \sum_{(f,g,h) \in \bar{J}}x_{f,g,h}\omega[f,g,h](p)\ =\ 0\,. \end{equation} By Gordan's Theorem,~\eqref{eq:pixleyzero} has a nonzero nonnegative solution if and only if the following system of strict inequalities is unsatisfiable: for all $(f,g,h) \in \bar{J}$, \begin{equation} \sum_{p \in P}y_p\omega[f,g,h](p)\ >\ 0\,. \end{equation} Consider the case $\tuple{f,g,h}=\tuple{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}$. Then $\omega[f,g,h]=\omega$ and thus $\omega[f,g,h](p)=\omega(p)>0$ for all $p\in {\rm supp}(\omega)\cap P$, by the definition of $P$. Moreover, by~\eqref{eq:Pweights} \begin{equation} \sum_{p\in P}y_p\omega(p) \ =\ \sum_{p_1\in P_1}(y_{p_1}+y_{p_2}+y_{p_3})\omega(p_1)\,, \end{equation} where we denoted (with a slight abuse of notation) by $p_2$ and $p_3$ the related operations of $p_1$. For $\tuple{f,g,h} = \tuple{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}$ the LHS of~\eqref{eq:pixleygordan} is equal to~\eqref{eq:split}. Thus, for~\eqref{eq:pixleygordan} to hold in this case we must have at least one triple of related operations $\tuple{p_1,p_2,p_3} \in J$ with $y_{p_1} + y_{p_2} + y_{p_3} > 0$. Suppose $\tuple{p_1,p_2,p_3}\in J$ is chosen to maximise $y_{p_1} + y_{p_2} + y_{p_3}$. The left-hand side of \eqref{eq:pixleygordan} when $\tuple{f,g,h} = \tuple{p_1,p_2,p_3}$ is equal to \begin{equation} - y_{p_1} - y_{p_2} - y_{p_3} + \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s)\,, \end{equation} since $o[p_1,p_2,p_3]$ is equal to a Pixley operation only when $o$ is one of the three projections, which give the first three terms in~\eqref{eq:abc}, or a semiprojection, which gives the last term of~\eqref{eq:abc}, the sum over $S$. We have \begin{equation} \begin{split} \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s)\ =\ & \sum_{s_1\in S_1}y_{s_1[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s_1) + \sum_{s_2\in S_2}y_{s_2[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s_2) + \sum_{s_3\in S_3}y_{s_3[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s_3) \\ =\ & \sum_{\substack{\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}\in S_1\times S_2\times S_3\\s_1,s_2,s_3\mbox{ \scriptsize related}}}(y_{s_1[p_1,p_2,p_3]}+y_{s_2[p_1,p_2,p_3]}+y_{s_3[p_1,p_2,p_3]})\omega(s_1) \\ \leq\ & \frac{\omega(S)}{3}(y_{p_1}+y_{p_2}+y_{p_3}),\\ \end{split} \end{equation} where the first equality follows from the definition of $S$; the second equality follows from fact that $s[p_1,p_2,p_3]$ is a Pixley operation of type $i$ given $s$ is a semiprojection of type $i$, where $i\in\{1,2,3\}$, and hence $\tuple{s_1[p_1,p_2,p_3],s_2[p_1,p_2,p_3],s_3[p_1,p_2,p_3]}$ is a triple of related Pixley operations given that $\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}$ is a triple of related semiprojections; and the last inequality follows from the definition of $w(S)$ and the choice of $(p_1,p_2,p_3)$. Combining~\eqref{eq:abc} and~\eqref{eq:S3}, we have \begin{equation} - y_{p_1} - y_{p_2} - y_{p_3} + \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s) \ \leq\ - y_{p_1} - y_{p_2} - y_{p_3} + \frac{w(S)}{3}(y_{p_1}+y_{p_2}+y_{p_3}) \ <\ 0\,, \end{equation} where the last strict inequality follows from $w(S)<3$ since $w(P)>0$ and~\eqref{eq:sum3}. Hence, \eqref{eq:pixleygordan} is unsatisfiable and, by Gordan's Theorem, \eqref{eq:pixleyzero} must have a nonzero nonnegative solution $x^*$. We finish Step~I by using $x^*$ to prove the existence of a weighting in $W$ that assigns zero weight to all Pixley operations. Let \begin{equation} \mu'=\sum_{(f,g,h) \in \bar{J}}x^*_{f,g,h}\omega[f,g,h]\,, \end{equation} be a weighted sum of superpositions of $\omega$. By the choice of $x^*$, $\mu'$ assigns zero weight to all Pixley operations. From the definition of $\bar{J}$, \begin{equation} \mu'\ =\ x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3]+\sum_{(f,g,h)\in J}x^*_{f,g,h}\omega[f,g,h]\,. \end{equation} We know that $x^*$ is nonzero and nonnegative. Note that $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}>0$ and $x^*_{f,g,h}=0$ for all $(f,g,h)\in J$ would contradict that $\mu'$ assigns zero weight to all Pixley operations. Let $(f,g,h)\in J$ and $i\in\{1,2,3\}$. Then $o[f,g,h]$ is a Pixley operation of type $i$ if $o$ is a semiprojection of type $i$, $o[f,g,h]$ is a semiprojection of type $i$ if $o$ is a Pixley operation of type $i$, $o[f,g,h]$ is a majority operation if $o$ is a minority operation, and finally $o[f,g,h]$ is a minority operation if $o$ is a majority operation. It follows that $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}=0$ would contradict that $\mu'$ assigns zero weight all Pixley operations since Pixley operations of type $i$ would be assigned negative weight since $w(S)-3<0$ as $w(P)>0$. Thus $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}>0$ and $x^*_{f,g,h}>0$ for at least one $(f,g,h)\in J$. Consequently, $\mu'$ is a nonzero weighting that assigns zero weight to all Pixley operations. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:sumofsuperpos}, $\mu'\in W$.
nodes.statement_short: Use Gordan's theorem to build a weighting in $W$ with zero weight on all Pixley operations.

nodes.name: Goal of Step I
nodes.statement: \textbf{Step I}: Eliminating Pixley operations. We now show how to eliminate Pixley operations if needed, that is, assume $w(P)>0$ and thus some operations from $P$ are assigned positive weight.
nodes.statement_short: Assume $w(P)>0$; aim to eliminate Pixley operations.

nodes.name: Case: only Pixley operations
nodes.statement: First assume that $\omega$ assigns positive weight to only Pixley operations, that is, ${\rm supp}(\omega)\subseteq P$. Hence $w(P)=3$. Take arbitrary $p_1,p'_1\in P_1$, $p_2,p'_2\in P_2$, and $p_3,p'_3\in P_3$. The following claims can be verified from the definitions: $p_1[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,p'_1]$ is a majority operation, $p_2[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,p'_1]=\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1$, and $p_3[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,p'_1]=\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2$. Consequently, $\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,p'_1]$ assigns weight $-1$ to $p'_1$, $+1$ to majority operations, and $0$ otherwise. Similarly, $\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,p'_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3]$ assigns weight $-1$ to $p'_2$, $+1$ to majority operations, and $0$ otherwise. Finally, $\omega[p'_3,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3]$ assigns weight $-1$ to $p'_3$, $+1$ to majority operations, and $0$ otherwise. Overall, the weighting \begin{equation} \mu\ =\ \omega+\sum_{p\in P_1}\omega(p)\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,p] +\sum_{p\in P_2}\omega(p)\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,p,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3] +\sum_{p\in P_3}\omega(p)\omega[p,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3] \end{equation} assigns weight $-1$ to each of the three ternary projections and weight $3$ to majority operations. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:sumofsuperpos}, the intermediate superpositions in~\eqref{eq:pixleyonly} can be improper as long as the resulting weighting $\mu$ is indeed a weighting. Thus $\mu\in W$ and case~(2a) of the theorem holds.
nodes.statement_short: Superpose to turn all Pixley weight into majority weight, giving case (2a).

nodes.name: Case: other operations too; linear system
nodes.statement: Let assume that ${\rm supp}(\omega)\not\subseteq P$, that is, $\omega$ assigns positive weight not only to Pixley operations. Let $J=\{(p_1,p_2,p_3)\in P_1\times P_2\times P_3\:|\:\mbox{$p_1, p_2, p_3$ are related}\}$ and $\bar{J}=\{(\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3)\}\cup J$. We consider the following linear system: for all Pixley operations $p\in P$, \begin{equation} \sum_{(f,g,h) \in \bar{J}}x_{f,g,h}\omega[f,g,h](p)\ =\ 0\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Define related triples $J$, $\bar J$ and the Pixley-zero linear system.

nodes.name: Apply Gordan
nodes.statement: By Gordan's Theorem,~\eqref{eq:pixleyzero} has a nonzero nonnegative solution if and only if the following system of strict inequalities is unsatisfiable: for all $(f,g,h) \in \bar{J}$, \begin{equation} \sum_{p \in P}y_p\omega[f,g,h](p)\ >\ 0\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The system has a nonnegative nonzero solution iff the dual strict system is unsatisfiable.

nodes.name: Identity triple
nodes.statement: Consider the case $\tuple{f,g,h}=\tuple{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}$. Then $\omega[f,g,h]=\omega$ and thus $\omega[f,g,h](p)=\omega(p)>0$ for all $p\in {\rm supp}(\omega)\cap P$, by the definition of $P$. Moreover, by~\eqref{eq:Pweights} \begin{equation} \sum_{p\in P}y_p\omega(p) \ =\ \sum_{p_1\in P_1}(y_{p_1}+y_{p_2}+y_{p_3})\omega(p_1)\,, \end{equation} where we denoted (with a slight abuse of notation) by $p_2$ and $p_3$ the related operations of $p_1$.
nodes.statement_short: For the identity triple the dual LHS splits over related triples.

nodes.name: Some related triple has positive $y$-sum
nodes.statement: For $\tuple{f,g,h} = \tuple{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}$ the LHS of~\eqref{eq:pixleygordan} is equal to~\eqref{eq:split}. Thus, for~\eqref{eq:pixleygordan} to hold in this case we must have at least one triple of related operations $\tuple{p_1,p_2,p_3} \in J$ with $y_{p_1} + y_{p_2} + y_{p_3} > 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Dual feasibility forces a related triple with positive $y$-sum.

nodes.name: Maximising triple
nodes.statement: Suppose $\tuple{p_1,p_2,p_3}\in J$ is chosen to maximise $y_{p_1} + y_{p_2} + y_{p_3}$. The left-hand side of \eqref{eq:pixleygordan} when $\tuple{f,g,h} = \tuple{p_1,p_2,p_3}$ is equal to \begin{equation} - y_{p_1} - y_{p_2} - y_{p_3} + \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s)\,, \end{equation} since $o[p_1,p_2,p_3]$ is equal to a Pixley operation only when $o$ is one of the three projections, which give the first three terms in~\eqref{eq:abc}, or a semiprojection, which gives the last term of~\eqref{eq:abc}, the sum over $S$.
nodes.statement_short: Pick the triple maximising the $y$-sum and expand the dual LHS there.

nodes.name: Bound semiprojection contribution
nodes.statement: We have \begin{equation} \begin{split} \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s)\ =\ & \sum_{s_1\in S_1}y_{s_1[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s_1) + \sum_{s_2\in S_2}y_{s_2[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s_2) + \sum_{s_3\in S_3}y_{s_3[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s_3) \\ =\ & \sum_{\substack{\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}\in S_1\times S_2\times S_3\\s_1,s_2,s_3\mbox{ \scriptsize related}}}(y_{s_1[p_1,p_2,p_3]}+y_{s_2[p_1,p_2,p_3]}+y_{s_3[p_1,p_2,p_3]})\omega(s_1) \\ \leq\ & \frac{\omega(S)}{3}(y_{p_1}+y_{p_2}+y_{p_3}),\\ \end{split} \end{equation} where the first equality follows from the definition of $S$; the second equality follows from fact that $s[p_1,p_2,p_3]$ is a Pixley operation of type $i$ given $s$ is a semiprojection of type $i$, where $i\in\{1,2,3\}$, and hence $\tuple{s_1[p_1,p_2,p_3],s_2[p_1,p_2,p_3],s_3[p_1,p_2,p_3]}$ is a triple of related Pixley operations given that $\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}$ is a triple of related semiprojections; and the last inequality follows from the definition of $w(S)$ and the choice of $(p_1,p_2,p_3)$.
nodes.statement_short: The semiprojection sum is at most $w(S)/3$ times the maximal $y$-sum.

nodes.name: Dual LHS negative
nodes.statement: Combining~\eqref{eq:abc} and~\eqref{eq:S3}, we have \begin{equation} - y_{p_1} - y_{p_2} - y_{p_3} + \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[p_1,p_2,p_3]}\omega(s) \ \leq\ - y_{p_1} - y_{p_2} - y_{p_3} + \frac{w(S)}{3}(y_{p_1}+y_{p_2}+y_{p_3}) \ <\ 0\,, \end{equation} where the last strict inequality follows from $w(S)<3$ since $w(P)>0$ and~\eqref{eq:sum3}.
nodes.statement_short: Since $w(S)<3$, the dual LHS is negative at the maximising triple.

nodes.name: Primal solution exists
nodes.statement: Hence, \eqref{eq:pixleygordan} is unsatisfiable and, by Gordan's Theorem, \eqref{eq:pixleyzero} must have a nonzero nonnegative solution $x^*$.
nodes.statement_short: By Gordan's theorem the Pixley-zero system has a solution $x^*$.

nodes.name: Define $\mu'$
nodes.statement: We finish Step~I by using $x^*$ to prove the existence of a weighting in $W$ that assigns zero weight to all Pixley operations. Let \begin{equation} \mu'=\sum_{(f,g,h) \in \bar{J}}x^*_{f,g,h}\omega[f,g,h]\,, \end{equation} be a weighted sum of superpositions of $\omega$. By the choice of $x^*$, $\mu'$ assigns zero weight to all Pixley operations.
nodes.statement_short: Form $\mu'$ from $x^*$; it gives zero weight to Pixley operations.

nodes.name: Split $\mu'$
nodes.statement: From the definition of $\bar{J}$, \begin{equation} \mu'\ =\ x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3]+\sum_{(f,g,h)\in J}x^*_{f,g,h}\omega[f,g,h]\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Separate the identity term from the related-triple terms.

nodes.name: Related triples needed
nodes.statement: We know that $x^*$ is nonzero and nonnegative. Note that $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}>0$ and $x^*_{f,g,h}=0$ for all $(f,g,h)\in J$ would contradict that $\mu'$ assigns zero weight to all Pixley operations.
nodes.statement_short: Using only the identity term would leave positive Pixley weight.

nodes.name: Effect of related-triple superposition
nodes.statement: Let $(f,g,h)\in J$ and $i\in\{1,2,3\}$. Then $o[f,g,h]$ is a Pixley operation of type $i$ if $o$ is a semiprojection of type $i$, $o[f,g,h]$ is a semiprojection of type $i$ if $o$ is a Pixley operation of type $i$, $o[f,g,h]$ is a majority operation if $o$ is a minority operation, and finally $o[f,g,h]$ is a minority operation if $o$ is a majority operation.
nodes.statement_short: Superposing with a related Pixley triple swaps types as described.

nodes.name: Conclude Step I
nodes.statement: It follows that $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}=0$ would contradict that $\mu'$ assigns zero weight all Pixley operations since Pixley operations of type $i$ would be assigned negative weight since $w(S)-3<0$ as $w(P)>0$. Thus $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}>0$ and $x^*_{f,g,h}>0$ for at least one $(f,g,h)\in J$. Consequently, $\mu'$ is a nonzero weighting that assigns zero weight to all Pixley operations. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:sumofsuperpos}, $\mu'\in W$.
nodes.statement_short: Both kinds of terms are needed, so $\mu'$ is a nonzero weighting in $W$ with no Pixley weight.

nodes.name: Step II: eliminating semiprojections
nodes.statement: \textbf{Step II}: Eliminating semiprojections. We now show how to eliminate semiprojections if needed. If $\mu'$ obtained in Step I assigns positive weight to only semiprojections then we are in case (3) (with $k$=3) of the theorem. Thus let assume that $\mu'$ assigns positive weight to semiprojections and at least one majority or minority operation. By Lemma~\ref{lem:perm}, we can assume the existence of a ternary weighting $\omega\in W$ which assigns weight -1 to all three projections (and thus assigns total positive weight 3). We will use the same notation for $S$, $S_1$, $S_2$, and $S_3$ as before although note that the weighting $\omega$ is now different from the one we had before and throughout Step I. We have $w(S)<3$ and~\eqref{eq:Srelated},~\eqref{eq:Scard},~\eqref{eq:Sweights} still hold for $\omega$. We again use Gordan's Theorem to show that there exists a nonzero ternary weighting in $W$ that assigns positive weight to majority and minority operations only. Let $J=\{(s_1,s_2,s_3)\in S_1\times S_2\times S_3\:|\:\mbox{$s_1, s_2, s_3$ are related}\}$ and $\bar{J}=\{(\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3)\}\cup J$. We consider the following linear system: for all semiprojections $s\in S$, \begin{equation} \sum_{\tuple{f,g,h}\in \bar{J}}x_{f,g,h}\omega[f,g,h](s)\ =\ 0\,. \end{equation} By Gordan's Theorem,~\eqref{eq:semiprojzero} has a nonzero nonnegative solution if and only if the following system of strict inequalities is unsatisfiable: for all $(f,g,h) \in \bar{J}$, \begin{equation} \sum_{s \in S}y_s\omega[f,g,h](s)\ >\ 0\,. \end{equation} As in Step I, we can argue that~\eqref{eq:semiprojgordan} is unsatisfiable. Consider the case $\tuple{f,g,h}=\tuple{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}$. Then $\omega[f,g,h]=\omega$ and thus $\omega[f,g,h](s)=\omega(s)>0$ for all $s\in{\rm supp}(\omega)\cap S$, by the definition of $S$. Moreover, by~\eqref{eq:Sweights} \begin{equation} \sum_{s\in S}\omega(s)y_s \ =\ \sum_{s_1\in S_1}(y_{s_1}+y_{s_2}+y_{s_3})\omega(s_1)\,, \end{equation} where we denoted by $s_2$ and $s_3$ the related operations of $s_1$. Therefore, for \eqref{eq:semiprojgordan} to hold when $\tuple{f,g,h} = \tuple{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}$ we must have at least one triple of related semiprojections $\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3} \in J$ with $y_{s_1} + y_{s_2} + y_{s_3} > 0$. Suppose $\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}\in J$ is chosen to maximise $y_{s_1} + y_{s_2} + y_{s_3}$. The left-hand side of \eqref{eq:semiprojgordan} when $\tuple{f,g,h} = \tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}$ is equal to \begin{equation} - y_{s_1} - y_{s_2} - y_{s_3} + \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[s_1,s_2,s_3]}\omega(s)\,, \end{equation} since $o[s_1,s_2,s_3]$ is equal to a semiprojection only when $o$ is one of the three projections, which give the first three terms in~\eqref{eq:Sabc}, or a semiprojection, which gives the last term of~\eqref{eq:Sabc}, the sum over $S$. We have \begin{equation} \begin{split} \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[s_1,s_2,s_3]}\omega(s)\ =\ & \sum_{s_1\in S_1}y_{s_1[s_1,s_2,s_3]}\omega(s_1) + \sum_{s_2\in S_2}y_{s_2[s_1,s_2,s_3]}\omega(s_2) + \sum_{s_3\in S_3}y_{s_3[s_1,s_2,s_3]}\omega(s_3) \\ =\ & \sum_{\substack{\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}\in S_1\times S_2\times S_3\\s_1,s_2,s_3\mbox{\scriptsize related}}}(y_{s_1[s_1,s_2,s_3]}+y_{s_2[s_1,s_2,s_3]}+y_{s_3[s_1,s_2,s_3]})\omega(s_1) \\ \leq\ & \frac{\omega(S)}{3}(y_{s_1}+y_{s_2}+y_{s_3}),\\ \end{split} \end{equation} where the first equality follows from the definition of $S$; the second equality follows from fact that $s[s_1,s_2,s_3]$ is a semiprojection of type $i$ given $s$ is a semiprojection of type $i$, where $i\in\{1,2,3\}$, and hence $\tuple{s_1[s_1,s_2,s_3],s_2[s_1,s_2,s_3],s_3[s_1,s_2,s_3]}$ is a triple of related semiprojections given that $\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}$ is a triple of related semiprojections; and the last inequality follows from the definition of $w(S)$ and the choice of $(s_1,s_2,s_3)$. Combining~\eqref{eq:Sabc} and~\eqref{eq:SS3}, we have \begin{equation} - y_{s_1} - y_{s_2} - y_{s_3} + \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[s_1,s_2,s_3]}\omega(s) \ \leq\ - y_{s_1} - y_{s_2} - y_{s_3} + \frac{w(S)}{3}(y_{s_1}+y_{s_2}+y_{s_3}) \ <\ 0\,, \end{equation} where the last strict inequality follows from $w(S)<3$. Hence, \eqref{eq:semiprojgordan} is unsatisfiable and, by Gordan's Theorem, \eqref{eq:semiprojzero} must have a nonzero nonnegative solution $x^*$. We finish Step~II by using $x^*$ to prove the existence of a weighting in $W$ that assigns zero weight to all semiprojections. Let \begin{equation} \mu=\sum_{(f,g,h) \in J}\omega[f,g,h]x^*_{f,g,h}\,, \end{equation} be a weighted sum of superpositions of $\omega$. By the choice of $x^*$, $\mu$ assigns zero weight to all semiprojections. From the definition of $\bar{J}$, \begin{equation} \mu\ =\ x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3]+\sum_{(f,g,h) \in J}x^*_{f,g,h}\omega[f,g,h]\,. \end{equation} We know that $x^*$ is nonzero and nonnegative. Note that $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}>0$ and $x^*_{f,g,h}=0$ for all $(f,g,h)\in J$ would contradict that $\mu'$ assigns zero weight to all semiprojections. Let $(s_1,s_2,s_3)\in J$ and $i\in\{1,2,3\}$. Then $o[s_1,s_2,s_3]$ is a semiprojection of type $i$ if $o$ is a semiprojection of type $i$, $o[s_1,s_2,s_3]$ is a majority operation if $o$ is a majority operation, and finally $o[s_1,s_2,s_3]$ is a minority operation if $o$ is a minority operation. (Note that we do not need to consider the case when $f$ is a Pixley operation as $\omega$ assigns zero weight to all Pixley operations.) It follows that $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}=0$ would contradict that $\mu$ assigns zero weight all semiprojections since semiprojections of type $i$ would be assigned negative weight since $w(S)-3<0$ as $\omega$ assigns positive weight to some majority or minority (or possibly both) operations. Thus $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}>0$ and $x^*_{f,g,h}$ for at least one $(f,g,h)\in J$. Consequently, $\mu$ is a nonzero weighting that assigns zero weight to all semiprojections. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:sumofsuperpos}, $\mu\in W$.
nodes.statement_short: Repeat the Gordan argument to obtain a weighting with zero weight on semiprojections.

nodes.name: Goal of Step II
nodes.statement: \textbf{Step II}: Eliminating semiprojections. We now show how to eliminate semiprojections if needed. If $\mu'$ obtained in Step I assigns positive weight to only semiprojections then we are in case (3) (with $k$=3) of the theorem. Thus let assume that $\mu'$ assigns positive weight to semiprojections and at least one majority or minority operation.
nodes.statement_short: If only semiprojections remain, case (3) holds; otherwise eliminate them.

nodes.name: Normalise via Lemma 2
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:perm}, we can assume the existence of a ternary weighting $\omega\in W$ which assigns weight -1 to all three projections (and thus assigns total positive weight 3). We will use the same notation for $S$, $S_1$, $S_2$, and $S_3$ as before although note that the weighting $\omega$ is now different from the one we had before and throughout Step I.
nodes.statement_short: Assume a ternary weighting with $-1$ on projections.

nodes.name: Recall equalities
nodes.statement: We have $w(S)<3$ and~\eqref{eq:Srelated},~\eqref{eq:Scard},~\eqref{eq:Sweights} still hold for $\omega$.
nodes.statement_short: The semiprojection weight relations still hold and $w(S)<3$.

nodes.name: Plan
nodes.statement: We again use Gordan's Theorem to show that there exists a nonzero ternary weighting in $W$ that assigns positive weight to majority and minority operations only.
nodes.statement_short: Plan: Gordan's theorem gives a weighting on majority and minority only.

nodes.name: Semiprojection linear system
nodes.statement: Let $J=\{(s_1,s_2,s_3)\in S_1\times S_2\times S_3\:|\:\mbox{$s_1, s_2, s_3$ are related}\}$ and $\bar{J}=\{(\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3)\}\cup J$. We consider the following linear system: for all semiprojections $s\in S$, \begin{equation} \sum_{\tuple{f,g,h}\in \bar{J}}x_{f,g,h}\omega[f,g,h](s)\ =\ 0\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Define related semiprojection triples and the semiprojection-zero system.

nodes.name: Apply Gordan
nodes.statement: By Gordan's Theorem,~\eqref{eq:semiprojzero} has a nonzero nonnegative solution if and only if the following system of strict inequalities is unsatisfiable: for all $(f,g,h) \in \bar{J}$, \begin{equation} \sum_{s \in S}y_s\omega[f,g,h](s)\ >\ 0\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to unsatisfiability of the dual strict system.

nodes.name: Identity triple
nodes.statement: As in Step I, we can argue that~\eqref{eq:semiprojgordan} is unsatisfiable. Consider the case $\tuple{f,g,h}=\tuple{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}$. Then $\omega[f,g,h]=\omega$ and thus $\omega[f,g,h](s)=\omega(s)>0$ for all $s\in{\rm supp}(\omega)\cap S$, by the definition of $S$. Moreover, by~\eqref{eq:Sweights} \begin{equation} \sum_{s\in S}\omega(s)y_s \ =\ \sum_{s_1\in S_1}(y_{s_1}+y_{s_2}+y_{s_3})\omega(s_1)\,, \end{equation} where we denoted by $s_2$ and $s_3$ the related operations of $s_1$.
nodes.statement_short: For the identity triple the dual LHS splits over related triples.

nodes.name: Positive $y$-sum triple
nodes.statement: Therefore, for \eqref{eq:semiprojgordan} to hold when $\tuple{f,g,h} = \tuple{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}$ we must have at least one triple of related semiprojections $\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3} \in J$ with $y_{s_1} + y_{s_2} + y_{s_3} > 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Some related triple has positive $y$-sum.

nodes.name: Maximising triple
nodes.statement: Suppose $\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}\in J$ is chosen to maximise $y_{s_1} + y_{s_2} + y_{s_3}$. The left-hand side of \eqref{eq:semiprojgordan} when $\tuple{f,g,h} = \tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}$ is equal to \begin{equation} - y_{s_1} - y_{s_2} - y_{s_3} + \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[s_1,s_2,s_3]}\omega(s)\,, \end{equation} since $o[s_1,s_2,s_3]$ is equal to a semiprojection only when $o$ is one of the three projections, which give the first three terms in~\eqref{eq:Sabc}, or a semiprojection, which gives the last term of~\eqref{eq:Sabc}, the sum over $S$.
nodes.statement_short: Pick the maximising triple and expand the dual LHS.

nodes.name: Bound semiprojection contribution
nodes.statement: We have \begin{equation} \begin{split} \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[s_1,s_2,s_3]}\omega(s)\ =\ & \sum_{s_1\in S_1}y_{s_1[s_1,s_2,s_3]}\omega(s_1) + \sum_{s_2\in S_2}y_{s_2[s_1,s_2,s_3]}\omega(s_2) + \sum_{s_3\in S_3}y_{s_3[s_1,s_2,s_3]}\omega(s_3) \\ =\ & \sum_{\substack{\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}\in S_1\times S_2\times S_3\\s_1,s_2,s_3\mbox{\scriptsize related}}}(y_{s_1[s_1,s_2,s_3]}+y_{s_2[s_1,s_2,s_3]}+y_{s_3[s_1,s_2,s_3]})\omega(s_1) \\ \leq\ & \frac{\omega(S)}{3}(y_{s_1}+y_{s_2}+y_{s_3}),\\ \end{split} \end{equation} where the first equality follows from the definition of $S$; the second equality follows from fact that $s[s_1,s_2,s_3]$ is a semiprojection of type $i$ given $s$ is a semiprojection of type $i$, where $i\in\{1,2,3\}$, and hence $\tuple{s_1[s_1,s_2,s_3],s_2[s_1,s_2,s_3],s_3[s_1,s_2,s_3]}$ is a triple of related semiprojections given that $\tuple{s_1,s_2,s_3}$ is a triple of related semiprojections; and the last inequality follows from the definition of $w(S)$ and the choice of $(s_1,s_2,s_3)$.
nodes.statement_short: The semiprojection sum is at most $w(S)/3$ times the maximal $y$-sum.

nodes.name: Dual LHS negative
nodes.statement: Combining~\eqref{eq:Sabc} and~\eqref{eq:SS3}, we have \begin{equation} - y_{s_1} - y_{s_2} - y_{s_3} + \sum_{s \in S}y_{s[s_1,s_2,s_3]}\omega(s) \ \leq\ - y_{s_1} - y_{s_2} - y_{s_3} + \frac{w(S)}{3}(y_{s_1}+y_{s_2}+y_{s_3}) \ <\ 0\,, \end{equation} where the last strict inequality follows from $w(S)<3$.
nodes.statement_short: Since $w(S)<3$, the dual LHS is negative.

nodes.name: Primal solution exists
nodes.statement: Hence, \eqref{eq:semiprojgordan} is unsatisfiable and, by Gordan's Theorem, \eqref{eq:semiprojzero} must have a nonzero nonnegative solution $x^*$.
nodes.statement_short: By Gordan's theorem the semiprojection-zero system has a solution.

nodes.name: Define $\mu$
nodes.statement: We finish Step~II by using $x^*$ to prove the existence of a weighting in $W$ that assigns zero weight to all semiprojections. Let \begin{equation} \mu=\sum_{(f,g,h) \in J}\omega[f,g,h]x^*_{f,g,h}\,, \end{equation} be a weighted sum of superpositions of $\omega$. By the choice of $x^*$, $\mu$ assigns zero weight to all semiprojections.
nodes.statement_short: Form $\mu$ from $x^*$; zero weight on semiprojections.

nodes.name: Split $\mu$
nodes.statement: From the definition of $\bar{J}$, \begin{equation} \mu\ =\ x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3]+\sum_{(f,g,h) \in J}x^*_{f,g,h}\omega[f,g,h]\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Separate identity and related-triple terms.

nodes.name: Related triples needed
nodes.statement: We know that $x^*$ is nonzero and nonnegative. Note that $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}>0$ and $x^*_{f,g,h}=0$ for all $(f,g,h)\in J$ would contradict that $\mu'$ assigns zero weight to all semiprojections.
nodes.statement_short: The identity term alone cannot cancel semiprojection weight.

nodes.name: Effect of related-semiprojection superposition
nodes.statement: Let $(s_1,s_2,s_3)\in J$ and $i\in\{1,2,3\}$. Then $o[s_1,s_2,s_3]$ is a semiprojection of type $i$ if $o$ is a semiprojection of type $i$, $o[s_1,s_2,s_3]$ is a majority operation if $o$ is a majority operation, and finally $o[s_1,s_2,s_3]$ is a minority operation if $o$ is a minority operation. (Note that we do not need to consider the case when $f$ is a Pixley operation as $\omega$ assigns zero weight to all Pixley operations.)
nodes.statement_short: Superposition preserves semiprojection, majority and minority types.

nodes.name: Conclude Step II
nodes.statement: It follows that $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}=0$ would contradict that $\mu$ assigns zero weight all semiprojections since semiprojections of type $i$ would be assigned negative weight since $w(S)-3<0$ as $\omega$ assigns positive weight to some majority or minority (or possibly both) operations. Thus $x^*_{\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_2,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_3}>0$ and $x^*_{f,g,h}$ for at least one $(f,g,h)\in J$. Consequently, $\mu$ is a nonzero weighting that assigns zero weight to all semiprojections. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:sumofsuperpos}, $\mu\in W$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mu$ is a nonzero weighting in $W$ with no semiprojection weight.

nodes.name: Step III: majority and minority operations
nodes.statement: \textbf{Step III}: Majority and minority operations. In Steps I and II, we have shown that any weighted clone $W$ with a positive ternary weighting contains a ternary weighting that assigns nonzero weight to semiprojections alone (case~(3) of the theorem with $k=3$), or a mix of majority and minority operations. Finally, we will show that if $W$ contains a weighting $\omega$ that assigns weight to majority and minority operations alone then $W$ also contains a weighting of one of the three types described in cases~(2a),~(2b), and~(2c) of the theorem. Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ denote the sets of majority and minority operations in the support of $\omega$. Suppose that $\omega$ assigns total weight $2+a$ to $M_1$ and total weight $1-a$ to $M_2$ for some $a > 0$. For each $f \in M_2$, we define $\mu_f = \omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,f]$, so $\mu_f$ assigns weight $a$ to $\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1$ and weight $-a$ to $f$. Note that $\mu_f$ is not a proper weighting, since $a > 0$. We obtain a weighting $\mu \in W$ which assigns positive weight to majority operations only as follows: \begin{equation} \mu = \omega + \sum_{f \in M_2}\frac{\omega(f)}{a}\mu_f\,. \end{equation} Similarly, suppose that $\omega$ assigns total weight $2-a$ to $M_1$ and total weight $1+a$ to $M_2$ for some $a>0$. For each $f\in M_1$, we define $\mu_f=\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,f,f]$, so $\mu_f$ assigns weight $a$ to $\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1$ and weight $-a$ to $f$. We obtain a weighting $\mu \in W$ which assigns positive weight to minority operations only as follows: \begin{equation} \mu = \omega + \sum_{f \in M_1}\frac{\omega(f)}{a}\mu_f\,. \end{equation} In both cases $\mu\in W$ by Lemma~\ref{lemma:sumofsuperpos}.
nodes.statement_short: Rebalance majority/minority weight to reach (2a), (2b) or (2c).

nodes.name: Goal of Step III
nodes.statement: \textbf{Step III}: Majority and minority operations. In Steps I and II, we have shown that any weighted clone $W$ with a positive ternary weighting contains a ternary weighting that assigns nonzero weight to semiprojections alone (case~(3) of the theorem with $k=3$), or a mix of majority and minority operations. Finally, we will show that if $W$ contains a weighting $\omega$ that assigns weight to majority and minority operations alone then $W$ also contains a weighting of one of the three types described in cases~(2a),~(2b), and~(2c) of the theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Show a majority/minority weighting yields one of (2a)-(2c).

nodes.name: Excess majority weight
nodes.statement: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ denote the sets of majority and minority operations in the support of $\omega$. Suppose that $\omega$ assigns total weight $2+a$ to $M_1$ and total weight $1-a$ to $M_2$ for some $a > 0$. For each $f \in M_2$, we define $\mu_f = \omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,f]$, so $\mu_f$ assigns weight $a$ to $\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1$ and weight $-a$ to $f$. Note that $\mu_f$ is not a proper weighting, since $a > 0$. We obtain a weighting $\mu \in W$ which assigns positive weight to majority operations only as follows: \begin{equation} \mu = \omega + \sum_{f \in M_2}\frac{\omega(f)}{a}\mu_f\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: If majority weight exceeds 2, cancel minority operations to get case (2a).

nodes.name: Excess minority weight
nodes.statement: Similarly, suppose that $\omega$ assigns total weight $2-a$ to $M_1$ and total weight $1+a$ to $M_2$ for some $a>0$. For each $f\in M_1$, we define $\mu_f=\omega[\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1,f,f]$, so $\mu_f$ assigns weight $a$ to $\ensuremath{e}^{(3)}_1$ and weight $-a$ to $f$. We obtain a weighting $\mu \in W$ which assigns positive weight to minority operations only as follows: \begin{equation} \mu = \omega + \sum_{f \in M_1}\frac{\omega(f)}{a}\mu_f\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: If minority weight exceeds 1, cancel majority operations to get case (2b).

nodes.name: Membership in $W$
nodes.statement: In both cases $\mu\in W$ by Lemma~\ref{lemma:sumofsuperpos}.
nodes.statement_short: Both constructed weightings lie in $W$ by Lemma 3.
